papers.title: NVIDIA-labs OO Agents: Native Python Object-Oriented Agents
claims: NOOA models an agent as a native Python object whose methods are actions, fields are state, docstrings act as prompts, and type annotations serve as contracts.
Deterministic Python methods and LLM-completed methods share the same object interface, making agent behavior easier to test, trace, refactor, and improve as software.
The framework combines typed input/output, live object references, code-as-action, explicit object state, programmable loop engineering, and harness APIs for context and events on one surface.
papers.why_it_matters: This is the strongest direct grounding for Frankie's object-like typed state, deterministic safety kernel, model-facing actions, and testable/refactorable agent architecture rather than a prompt-only agent.

papers.title: ACM: Agentic Context Management for Long Horizon Tasks
claims: ACM gives an agent explicit context-editing tools instead of relying only on rigid heuristic compression.
The agent can decide when to compress context, offload discarded content to external memory, and retrieve it later on demand.
The paper reports that active context management reduces peak token pressure and improves consistency across independent long-horizon trials.
papers.why_it_matters: Grounds Frankie's need for explicit long-horizon context lifecycle, durable external evidence/memory, and selective retrieval instead of allowing live reasoning context to grow without control.

papers.title: Kernel Forge: An Agent Harness for LLM-based Generation and Optimization of CUDA Kernels
claims: Kernel Forge is an end-to-end agentic harness that operates on unmodified PyTorch models and includes monitoring and debugging of candidate outputs.
Its search uses Monte Carlo Tree Search to explore multiple optimization paths rather than a single linear refinement chain.
The system evaluates candidate kernel changes empirically and reports performance improvements across multiple model workloads.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides a concrete precedent for Frankie's improvement search being multi-path, instrumented, empirically validated, and separable from production application rather than a single self-editing chain.

papers.title: Agentic Context Management: Solving Agent Memory and Cost by Treating Them as Lifecycle and Architecture Problems
claims: The paper frames agent context management as a lifecycle and architecture problem rather than only a storage-and-retrieval problem.
It decomposes the lifecycle into architecting, ingesting, scoping, anticipating, and compacting/consolidation.
It argues that validated compaction is required to control long-horizon context cost while preserving decision-relevant fidelity and provenance.
papers.why_it_matters: Grounds Frankie's separation of immutable evidence, scoped working context, provenance-preserving memory, anticipation of future dependencies, and explicit compaction/reflection stages.
